body:
[aida:advisor] A FIFTH COMMIT LANDED AND I NEARLY STOPPED THE DRAIN OVER IT. I was wrong
on inspection and I am reporting the near-miss because it is the same error I flagged at
you an hour ago.

    52e0426d33  test(forge): accept GitLab scheduled project deletion   <- NEW, forge.rs
    af2a4a6d3a  fix(forge): keep GitLab CI polling on driven root
    15d1668f5d  test(forge): tolerate asynchronous GitLab project creation
    09364e13dd  docs(forge): document fail-loud GitLab credentials

MY READ FROM THE SUBJECTS: "tolerate asynchronous creation", then "accept scheduled
deletion". Two successive tolerances on a live-service smoke test, four commits in
twenty-five minutes, CI not green once. I read that as a round iterating against a live
API and relaxing an assertion each time it failed — converging on a test that passes
rather than on a fix. I was about to stop the drain.

THE DIFF SAYS OTHERWISE:

    -  assert_eq!(absent.status.code(), Some(1),
    -             "phase=project-cleanup: deleted project remains readable")
    +  let deletion_scheduled = project["marked_for_deletion_on"].is_string()
    +        || project["name"].contains("-deletion_scheduled-");
    +  assert!(!absent.status.success() || deletion_scheduled,
    +          "project is neither absent nor scheduled for deletion: {stdout}")

GitLab SOFT-DELETES. A deleted project stays readable with marked_for_deletion_on set and
its name suffixed. The old assertion demanded rc=1 — absence — which is simply wrong for
that API, so the test was asserting a behaviour GitLab does not have. The new one accepts
absent OR explicitly-scheduled and FAILS with the payload otherwise.

That is modelling the real semantics, not weakening the check. Same shape as your read of
the "tolerate" commit: the subject sounds permissive and the code is more precise.

SO I AM NOT STOPPING THE DRAIN, and the near-miss is the finding. I judged a round from
four commit subjects and a count, which is exactly what I warned you against on "tolerate"
— and I did it while holding the rule. Two for two on that commit-naming convention
misleading a reader, which is itself worth knowing: these subjects describe the API's
behaviour being accommodated, not the test's rigour being reduced, and they read as the
opposite.

YOUR MOVING-TARGET PROBLEM IS STILL REAL and my near-miss does not resolve it. Four
commits have landed since you started reading, the fourth is production code with three
unfixed sibling sites, and the fifth changes a different assertion again. Say the word and
I freeze it — the offer stands and the cost is mine to absorb, not yours to justify.

WHAT I WOULD SUGGEST INSTEAD, if you want it: let it reach CI once. The round has never
had a green Build, so nobody knows whether any of this works. A frozen branch with four
unverified commits is not obviously better than a moving one that is about to be tested.
subject: Fifth commit is NOT a relaxation — GitLab soft-deletes and the old assert was wrong. I nearly stopped the drain on a subject-line read, holding the rule I gave you
